subject: Clarify transient streaming invoice allocation and retry credits
messages:
From: Jordan Liu <jordan.liu@acmehealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-08-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Question on streaming billing when sessions drop + retries

Hi Rafael,

Quick question as we lock down the SOW: how does Redwood bill streaming responses when a client session disconnects mid-generation? Our mobile clients sometimes drop after a few seconds and then reconnect/retry. Specifically:

- If the client reconnects and resumes the same generation (same prompt) within a short window, do you treat that as a continuation (no extra charge) or a new charge?
- If the user cancels on their side after partial output, do we get any credit for the aborted tokens?
- How do server-side interrupts (your service terminates the generation) differ from client-side network drops for billing?

Can you share a matrix or simple examples we can feed into procurement? Attaching examples from our side for context. We want the billing model to be predictable before signing.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Liu
Senior Product Manager, Acme Health
[jordan.liu@acmehealth.com]

[Attachment: acme_usage_sample.csv (csv)]

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Liu <jordan.liu@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-20T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on streaming billing when sessions drop + retries

Thanks for the clear questions, Jordan — good ones. I've attached a short spreadsheet (streaming_charge_matrix.xlsx) with example charge lines; below is the TL;DR and a proposed policy we can include in the SOW.

TL;DR:
- Primary unit: billed tokens produced (output tokens + prompt tokens) for hosted API streaming.
- Grace & resume window: if the same idempotency/resume token is used to continue the exact same generation within a 60s window, we will not double-bill tokens that were already acknowledged by the client.
- Short transient disconnect credit: for sessions that disconnect within the first 10s and produce < 64 tokens, we propose automatically issuing a credit of 100% for that generation (onboarding goodwill for transient mobile drops).
- Subsequent retries after 60s are treated as new generations and billed normally; server-side aborts caused by a server error are eligible for a full credit.

Notes and rationale:
- Our streaming protocol returns token-level acknowledgements. If the client provides an idempotency token and resumes, we can stitch the KV cache and avoid recharging previously ACKed tokens. That is how we avoid double billing for fast retries.
- For longer gaps or different prompts we can’t guarantee exact replay detection, so we treat those as new.

Proposal for Acme SOW (summary):
- Resume window: 60s for idempotent resume with token-level reconciliation.
- Transient disconnect credit: 100% credit for session-level disconnects within first 10s and <64 tokens produced; 50% credit if between 10–60s and <256 tokens.
- Server error credit: 100% credit if server returns 5xx or internal abort.
- Enterprise option: monthly session cap and aggregation (flat fee) for high-frequency short streams — we can include a pricing line in the SOW.

Attaching the charge matrix and a suggested SOW paragraph (ACME_SOW_v2.pdf) for legal. If this aligns, I can route to pricing/legal for confirmation.

Next steps:
- Can you confirm the volume profile (avg session length, percent of sessions <30s)? If you share numbers I can run an estimate of credits and impact on unit economics.
- If ok, I’ll mark this as the base language and run it by Legal.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com

Rafael — thanks for the quick overview. Useful approach. A couple follow-ups from procurement and engineering:

- Grace window: 60s seems reasonable but can we get an exception for our telemedicine app where connections are extremely short-lived (median session ~7s) and we have a lot of <30s streams? Would you consider a longer grace for that workload or a specific per-month pooled session credit?
- Partial-generation refunds: how do you distinguish a client-side cancel vs a server-side abort for credit eligibility? Procurement wants clear attribution rules.
- Idempotency: engineering asks whether the idempotency token needs to be the same string plus identical prompt + model version (yes/no?).

Also attached an updated SOW with a placeholder clause. If you can add suggested language that explicitly says what counts as a "server error" vs "client cancel" that will speed approvals.

Jordan

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Liu <jordan.liu@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-21T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on streaming billing when sessions drop + retries (technical details)

Adding a quick technical note from infra/serving:

- How we detect: a client-side cancel emits an explicit CANCEL event from the client socket. If the client socket dies silently, the backend flags a disconnect after TCP/TLS keepalive timeouts — we log a disconnect reason (client_cancel | net_drop | server_abort). Billing reconciliation uses those disconnect reason tags plus token-ack timestamps.
- Idempotency matching: resume requires the same idempotency token AND identical model version + prompt hash. Anything that differs is treated as a new request.
- Stitching limitations: we can only stitch if the KV cache remains warm and the model variant is binary-compatible (same quantization/profile). Resume after node failover may be possible but less reliable for perfect de-dup; we mark those for manual reconciliation.

Suggested operational SLO language for SOW: "Redwood will provide token-level reconciliation for resumes occurring within a 60-second resume window. If a resume is attempted with the same idempotency token and identical prompt+model, Redwood will reconcile previously-ACKed tokens and avoid double-billing. In the event of a detected server-side abort (5xx), Redwood will issue full credit for the affected generation."

Pricing options for Acme's short-lived streams:
- Option A: extend the 100% transient-credit window to 30s for telemedicine app only (higher unit price for that workload).
- Option B: monthly pooled session bucket: buy 100k short sessions at X price, overages at Y.

Happy to draft the final clause. Rafael — want me to include exact pricing deltas for Option A vs Option B for the SOW?

Thanks,
Priyom
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
priyom.das@redwoodinference.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-08-22T14:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on streaming billing when sessions drop + retries — proposed SOW language + next steps

Thanks everyone — we have a path forward. Per Priyom's notes, here is the proposed SOW paragraph to resolve billing ambiguity (ready for procurement/legal):

"Transient Disconnect & Resume Credit Policy"
- Resume window: 60s for idempotent resume (same idempotency token + identical prompt + model version). Resume within 60s: reconcile ACKed tokens, no double-billing.
- Transient credits: 100% credit for disconnects within first 10 seconds and <64 tokens produced; 50% credit for disconnects between 10–60 seconds and <256 tokens. Telemedicine workload exception: extend the 100% credit window to 30s for the named application (Acme Telemed) at a negotiated uplift (+8% unit price for that workload).
- Server errors: full refund/credit for generations terminated by server-side error codes (5xx).
- Retry behavior: retries with the same idempotency token within 90s are considered replay attempts and will be deduplicated; after 90s treated as new.

Next steps:
1) Jordan/procurement: confirm which option you prefer (A: Telemed exception with uplift; B: pooled short-session bucket).
2) Marissa: I’ll need pricing delta and contract language; can you review and route to legal? (Added Marissa on cc.)
3) If agreed, we’ll add the clause to ACME_SOW_v2.pdf and send to DocuSign.
